mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES mobility from -43.1 to -22.3 over the last week signals reinstated commuting and work-adjacent shopping trips, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as foot traffic near offices and transit hubs resumes.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 20.8 points in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week TRANSIT rebound exceeding 7 points indicates relaxed mobility restrictions or reopened transit capacity, which mechanically enables more retail visits within two weeks as commuters and shoppers regain access to transit-dependent retail corridors.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 7 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.7 to -26.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after a TRANSIT jump exceeding the 7-point threshold, or RETAIL_REC declines further despite the trigger firing.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous WORKPLACES rebound and RESIDENTIAL decline indicate a joint behavioral shift away from home-centered routines toward out-of-home activity; the interaction of these two series compounds to drive a stronger four-week increase in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 12.4 to 8.7 while WORKPLACES rose from -43.1 to -22.3
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's four-week forward mean does not exceed its backward mean despite concurrent WORKPLACES increase and RESIDENTIAL decrease, the interaction effect is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime where WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS mobility have all moved off their pandemic lows simultaneously, broad policy loosening acts as a common driver that lifts RETAIL_REC over four weeks; this mechanism is only active while multiple categories co-move upward.
candidate_trigger: at least two of WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, PARKS improve for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved markedly in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show sustained improvement, the regime-conditional policy mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The decline in PARKS mobility from its recent peak of 0.1 to -11.7 suggests a seasonal shift away from outdoor recreation, which should redirect leisure activity toward indoor retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 0.1 at t-2w to -11.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of a sustained PARKS decline, or if PARKS and RETAIL_REC move in the same direction, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC fell sharply from -18.0 to -24.4 in the most recent week, an outsized one-week drop inconsistent with the broader reopening trend in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT; this is expected to mean-revert upward within one week as the anomaly corrects.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC drops more than 5 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC dropped 6.4 points in the latest week despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improving
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat in the week following the anomalous drop, the mean-reversion hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained stable and mildly positive (6.6 to 8.6) while RETAIL_REC is volatile and negative, indicating households are maintaining essential-only shopping habits rather than resuming discretionary retail; this behavioral caution should keep RETAIL_REC flat-to-lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a narrow 6.6-8.6 band across four weeks while RETAIL_REC swung between -18.0 and -24.6
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks while GROCERY_PHARM remains flat, the essential-only behavioral caution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rebound simultaneously beyond 15 points from their recent trough, it signals a coordinated loosening of mobility restrictions that interacts to produce a disproportionately strong four-week RETAIL_REC increase, exceeding what either series predicts independently, but only while restrictions remain in an easing regime.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise more than 15 points from their four-week trough
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 27.1 points and TRANSIT rose 9.5 points from their respective troughs
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next four-week mean does not exceed its prior four-week mean despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT clearing the 15-point rebound threshold, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
